question.:question/problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix $M$ into the matrix $N$, where

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 2 & 0 \\ 4 & 6 & -5 \\ 5 & 6 & -5\end{bmatrix},\,N=\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 2 & 0 \\ \frac{20}{7} & \frac{30}{7} & - \frac{25}{7} \\ 5 & 6 & -5\end{bmatrix}?
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, notice that the $1$st and $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the $2$nd row.

By considering the given row operations that modify the $2$nd row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 2 & 0 \\ 4 & 6 & -5 \\ 5 & 6 & -5\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2}:=\frac{5}{7}{R}_{2} \\ & \sim\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 2 & 0 \\ \frac{20}{7} & \frac{30}{7} & - \frac{25}{7} \\ 5 & 6 & -5\end{bmatrix} \\ & =N.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{2}:=\frac{5}{7}{R}_{2}.
$$
